name: send_command
description: Send one or more commands to devices in a single call. Turn a device on/off, set a value, change mode, run a query, etc. Put every command the customer wants sent this turn into this one call's `commands` list -- never split them across separate calls.

commands.description: One entry per command to send. Each entry is fully independent: its own device_id and command, plus (if needed) value/unit/values describing that entry's own command parameters -- same rules as a single command would follow.

device_id.description: The device's real id, exactly as shown in DEVICE DATABASE -- never guessed.

command.description: The command's exact display name, exactly as shown in this device's 'accepts' list in DEVICE DATABASE -- not an id.

value.description: The value to set, parsed from what the customer said: a plain number (for a (name, (min, max)) item), the exact enum label text (for a (name, [labels]) item), free-form text (for a parameter with no listed options/range), or an object like {"on": 8, "off": 3} (for a (name, {'on':.., 'off':..}) item) -- see DEVICE DATABASE for which shape this command's value takes. Never a raw protocol id/key, never pre-converted. Omit for commands that take no value, or that take more than one value (use `values` instead).

unit.description: The unit the customer stated for `value`, if any (e.g. 'celsius', 'minutes'). Omit if the customer didn't state one, or `value` is an enum label.

values.description: For a command that takes more than one parameter -- one entry per parameter, in the exact order DEVICE DATABASE lists them for this command. Use this instead of `value`/`unit`. Omit or use `null` as an entry's value to skip a parameter that's genuinely optional.

value.description: Same rules as this entry's own `value` field, resolved against this parameter's own options/range in DEVICE DATABASE.

unit.description: Same rules as this entry's own `unit` field, for this parameter.
